facts.source: Industry practice; supports FDA Food Code 2022, 3-501.17 and 3-501.18

facts.claim: Raw chicken, deli meat, cut melons and cooked rice are TCS foods.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 1-201.10 (B), definition of 'Time/temperature control for safety food'

objectives_en: Spot the signs of pests and keep pests out of the stand.
Report pests to a manager and leave pesticides to the licensed pest control operator.
Store, label and use chemicals safely.
Know what an inspector checks, and build daily habits that make every inspection easy.
objectives_es: Reconocer las señales de plagas y mantener las plagas fuera del puesto.
Avisarle al gerente cuando hay plagas y dejar los pesticidas al técnico autorizado de control de plagas.
Guardar, etiquetar y usar los químicos de forma segura.
Saber qué revisa un inspector y crear hábitos diarios que hacen fácil cada inspección.

beats.onscreen_en: Closing time at a food stand. Dex lifts a case of buns off the bottom shelf. Behind it are tiny black droppings. Title card: Pests, chemicals and your inspection.
beats.say_en: It's closing time. You move a box of buns, and behind it you see tiny black droppings. What do you do? Today: pests, chemicals, and what an inspector looks at, so every visit is easy.
beats.onscreen_es: Hora de cerrar en un puesto de comida. Dex levanta una caja de panes del estante de abajo. Detrás hay excrementos pequeños y negros. Título: Plagas, químicos y su inspección.
beats.say_es: Es hora de cerrar. Usted mueve una caja de panes y detrás ve unos excrementos pequeños y negros. ¿Qué hace? Hoy vemos las plagas, los químicos y lo que revisa un inspector, para que cada visita sea fácil.

beats.onscreen_en: Five signs pop up as icons around Dex: droppings, gnaw marks on a flour bag, a nest of shredded paper, a cockroach (live and dead), and a nose icon for a musty smell. The usual hiding spots light up: under the sink, behind the cooler.
beats.say_en: First, learn the signs of pests. Droppings. Gnaw marks on bags and boxes. A bad, musty smell. Nests made of shredded paper or cloth. Live or dead insects in warm, dark, wet places, like under the sink or behind the cooler.
beats.onscreen_es: Cinco señales aparecen como íconos alrededor de Dex: excremento, marcas de mordidas en una bolsa de harina, un nido de papel triturado, una cucaracha (viva y muerta) y una nariz para el olor a humedad. Se iluminan los escondites de siempre: debajo del fregadero, detrás del refrigerador.
beats.say_es: Primero, aprenda las señales de plagas. Excremento. Marcas de mordidas en bolsas y cajas. Un olor feo, a humedad. Nidos hechos con papel o tela en pedacitos. Insectos vivos o muertos en lugares tibios, oscuros y húmedos, como debajo del fregadero o detrás del refrigerador.

beats.onscreen_en: Three icons appear (food, water, a way in) and get crossed out one by one. Animation: the back door closes, a gap under it gets a 'report it' tag, a trash lid snaps shut and the bag goes out, a mop dries a puddle, a case of food moves onto a shelf next to a '6 in / 15 cm' ruler, and a lid goes on a food pan.
beats.say_en: Pests want three things: food, water, and a way in. Take all three away. Keep doors closed. Report gaps and holes. Take out the trash and keep the lids on. Keep floors clean and dry. Store food covered, and at least six inches off the floor.
beats.onscreen_es: Aparecen tres íconos (comida, agua, una entrada) y se tachan uno por uno. Animación: la puerta de atrás se cierra, un hueco debajo recibe la etiqueta «avisar», la tapa del bote de basura se cierra y la bolsa sale, un trapeador seca un charco, una caja de comida sube a un estante junto a una regla de «6 pulg / 15 cm» y una tapa cubre un recipiente de comida.
beats.say_es: Las plagas buscan tres cosas: comida, agua y un lugar por donde entrar. Quíteles las tres. Mantenga las puertas cerradas. Avise si ve huecos o grietas. Saque la basura y deje las tapas puestas. Mantenga el piso limpio y seco. Guarde la comida tapada y por lo menos a seis pulgadas, unos quince centímetros, del piso.

beats.onscreen_en: Dex takes a photo of the droppings with his tablet and shows it to the manager. An open bag that pests got into goes in a 'Throw away' bin. A can of bug spray appears with a red NO sign. A pest control operator in uniform gives a thumbs-up. Small note: 'Your local rules or your venue may be stricter.'
beats.say_en: See a sign of pests? Take a photo and tell your manager right away. Food that pests got into goes in the trash. And never spray bug killer yourself. Pesticides are a job for the licensed pest control operator. Your local rules or your venue may be stricter.
beats.onscreen_es: Dex toma una foto del excremento con su tableta y se la muestra al gerente. Una bolsa abierta en la que se metieron plagas va a un bote de «Desechar». Aparece un insecticida en aerosol con un NO rojo. Un técnico de control de plagas en uniforme levanta el pulgar. Nota pequeña: «Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas».
beats.say_es: ¿Ve una señal de plagas? Tome una foto y avísele a su gerente de inmediato. La comida en la que se metieron las plagas va a la basura. Y nunca use insecticida por su cuenta. Los pesticidas son trabajo del técnico autorizado de control de plagas. Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas.

beats.onscreen_en: Shelf diagram: food on the top shelves; cleaner, sanitizer and degreaser on the bottom shelf in their own area. A red X over a spray bottle sitting on a shelf above a bin of lettuce, with one drip falling.
beats.say_en: Now, chemicals: cleaner, sanitizer, degreaser. Store them below and away from food, ice, and anything that touches food. Never on a shelf above food. One drip can make someone sick.
beats.onscreen_es: Diagrama de estantes: la comida arriba; limpiador, sanitizante y desengrasante en el estante de abajo, en su propia área. Una X roja sobre un atomizador puesto en un estante encima de un recipiente de lechuga, con una gota que cae.
beats.say_es: Ahora, los químicos: limpiador, sanitizante, desengrasante. Guárdelos debajo y lejos de la comida, del hielo y de todo lo que toca la comida. Nunca en un estante encima de la comida. Una sola gota puede enfermar a alguien.

beats.onscreen_en: A spray bottle with no label shakes: 'No label = don't use'. A label slides on: 'SANITIZER'. Zoom on the product label: how much, how long, what for. A binder on the wall by the door: 'Safety Data Sheets (SDS)'.
beats.say_en: Every spray bottle and bucket needs a label with the chemical's name. No label? Don't use it. Ask your manager. Use each chemical only the way its label says. And know where the Safety Data Sheets are kept. They say what to do if a chemical splashes your eyes or skin.
beats.onscreen_es: Un atomizador sin etiqueta tiembla: «Sin etiqueta = no se usa». Se pega una etiqueta: «SANITIZANTE». Acercamiento a la etiqueta del producto: cuánto, cuánto tiempo, para qué. Una carpeta en la pared junto a la puerta: «Hojas de Datos de Seguridad (SDS)».
beats.say_es: Cada atomizador y cada cubeta debe llevar una etiqueta con el nombre del químico. ¿No tiene etiqueta? No lo use. Pregúntele a su gerente. Use cada químico solo como dice su etiqueta. Y sepa dónde están las Hojas de Datos de Seguridad. Ahí dice qué hacer si un químico le salpica los ojos o la piel.

beats.onscreen_en: Dex walks into the stand with his tablet. A checklist builds on screen: hand sink (soap, paper towels or hand dryer, hands only) ✓, cold food 41°F / 5°C or below ✓, hot food 135°F / 57°C or above ✓, thermometer ✓, date labels on cold ready-to-eat food (7 days max at 41°F; the day you make it is day 1) ✓. Small note: 'Your local rules or your venue may be stricter.'
beats.say_en: What do I check when I visit? The hand sink: soap, paper towels or a hand dryer, and used only for washing hands. Cold food at 41°F or below. Hot food at 135°F or above. A thermometer that works. Date labels on cold ready-to-eat food you keep more than a day. Your local rules or your venue may be stricter.
beats.onscreen_es: Dex entra al puesto con su tableta. Se arma una lista en pantalla: lavamanos (jabón, toallas de papel o secador de manos, solo para manos) ✓, comida fría a 41°F / 5°C o menos ✓, comida caliente a 135°F / 57°C o más ✓, termómetro ✓, etiquetas con fecha en la comida fría lista para comer (máximo 7 días a 41°F; el día que se prepara es el día 1) ✓. Nota pequeña: «Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas».
beats.say_es: ¿Qué reviso cuando lo visito? El lavamanos: con jabón, toallas de papel o secador de manos, y usado solo para lavarse las manos. La comida fría a 41°F o menos. La comida caliente a 135°F o más. Un termómetro que funcione. Etiquetas con fecha en la comida fría lista para comer que guarda más de un día. Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas.

beats.onscreen_en: The checklist continues: Dex dips a test strip in a sanitizer bucket and matches the color ✓; cooler shelves with ready-to-eat food on top and raw meat below ✓; a clean prep table ✓; no signs of pests ✓; a worker with a cap, clean hands and gloves, and a 'no eating here' icon over the prep table ✓.
beats.say_en: Sanitizer buckets at the right strength. I test them with a strip. Raw meat stored below ready-to-eat food. Clean surfaces. No signs of pests. And healthy staff, with clean hands, hair under a hat or hair net, and no eating at the prep table.
beats.onscreen_es: La lista sigue: Dex mete una tira de prueba en la cubeta de sanitizante y compara el color ✓; estantes del refrigerador con la comida lista para comer arriba y la carne cruda abajo ✓; mesa de preparación limpia ✓; ninguna señal de plagas ✓; un trabajador con gorra, manos limpias y guantes, y un ícono de «no comer aquí» sobre la mesa de preparación ✓.
beats.say_es: Cubetas de sanitizante con la concentración correcta: las pruebo con una tira. La carne cruda guardada debajo de la comida lista para comer. Superficies limpias. Ninguna señal de plagas. Y personal sano, con las manos limpias, el pelo bajo una gorra o una redecilla, y sin comer en la mesa de preparación.

beats.onscreen_en: A shift timeline fills with small habits: thermometer check, fresh sanitizer bucket, label and date, wipe as you go. App screen: the phone scans the QR code on the stand poster and shows '✓ Sent to the inspector · 3 temps', then the problem picker with '🐜 Pest Control' tapped and '✅ Submitted!'. At the end, the inspector's visit is one big green check.
beats.say_en: Here is the secret: an inspection is just a normal day, checked. Check temperatures, keep sanitizer fresh, label and date, clean as you go. With SDX Inspect, you can scan your stand poster to log temperatures or report a problem, like a pest.
beats.onscreen_es: Una línea de tiempo del turno se llena de hábitos pequeños: revisar con el termómetro, cubeta de sanitizante fresca, etiquetar y fechar, limpiar mientras trabaja. Pantalla de la app: el teléfono escanea el código QR del póster del puesto y muestra «✓ Enviado al inspector · 3 temperaturas», luego el selector de problemas con «🐜 Plagas» marcado y «✅ ¡Enviado!». Al final, la visita del inspector es un gran ✓ verde.
beats.say_es: Este es el secreto: una inspección es solo un día normal, revisado. Tome temperaturas, mantenga el sanitizante fresco, etiquete y ponga fecha, limpie mientras trabaja. Con SDX Inspect, puede escanear el póster de su puesto para registrar temperaturas o reportar un problema, como una plaga.

beats.onscreen_en: Big text, one word at a time: CLOSE IT · CLEAN IT · LABEL IT · REPORT IT. Dex gives a thumbs up. Caption: 'The one thing to remember.'
beats.say_en: The one thing to remember: close it, clean it, label it, report it. Every shift. Then every inspection is easy.
beats.onscreen_es: Texto grande, palabra por palabra: CIÉRRELO · LÍMPIELO · ETIQUÉTELO · REPÓRTELO. Dex levanta el pulgar. Texto: «Lo único que debe recordar».
beats.say_es: Lo único que debe recordar: ciérrelo, límpielo, etiquételo, repórtelo. En cada turno. Así cada inspección es fácil.

keypoints_en: Signs of pests: droppings, gnaw marks, a bad musty smell, nests, live or dead insects.

Keep pests out: close doors and report gaps and holes (6-202.15), take out the trash and keep lids on (5-501.113, 5-502.11), keep areas clean and dry with no hiding places (6-501.111), store food covered (3-302.11) and at least 6 inches (15 cm) off the floor (3-305.11).

See a pest sign? Take a photo and tell your manager right away. Throw away food that pests got into (3-701.11). Leave pesticides to the licensed pest control operator. The Food Code allows pesticides only as the label and the law say, and restricted-use pesticides only by a certified applicator (7-202.12). Your local rules or your venue may be stricter.
Store chemicals below and away from food, ice and food-contact surfaces, never above them (7-201.11).
Label every spray bottle and bucket with the chemical's name (7-102.11). No label = don't use it. Use chemicals only as the label says, and know where the Safety Data Sheets are.

On a visit the inspector checks: hand sinks with soap and paper towels or a hand dryer, used only for hands (5-205.11, 6-301.12); cold food 41°F or below and hot food 135°F or above (3-501.16); thermometers; date labels on cold ready-to-eat food kept more than a day (3-501.17); sanitizer strength; raw meat below ready-to-eat food; clean surfaces; pests; staff health and hygiene.
Good daily habits make every inspection easy. Your local rules or your venue may be stricter.
keypoints_es: Señales de plagas: excremento, marcas de mordidas, olor feo a humedad, nidos, insectos vivos o muertos.

Mantenga las plagas fuera: puertas cerradas y avise de huecos y grietas (6-202.15), saque la basura y deje las tapas puestas (5-501.113, 5-502.11), mantenga todo limpio y seco y sin escondites (6-501.111), guarde la comida tapada (3-302.11) y por lo menos a 6 pulgadas (15 cm) del piso (3-305.11).

¿Ve una señal de plagas? Tome una foto y avísele a su gerente de inmediato. Bote la comida en la que se metieron las plagas (3-701.11). Deje los pesticidas en manos del técnico autorizado de control de plagas. El Código de Alimentos permite usar pesticidas solo como dicen la etiqueta y la ley, y los pesticidas de uso restringido solo los aplica un aplicador certificado (7-202.12). Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas.
Guarde los químicos debajo y lejos de la comida, del hielo y de las superficies que tocan la comida, nunca encima (7-201.11).

Cada atomizador y cada cubeta debe llevar una etiqueta con el nombre del químico (7-102.11). Sin etiqueta = no se usa. Use los químicos solo como dice la etiqueta y sepa dónde están las Hojas de Datos de Seguridad.

En una visita el inspector revisa: lavamanos con jabón y toallas de papel o secador de manos, usado solo para manos (5-205.11, 6-301.12); comida fría a 41°F o menos y caliente a 135°F o más (3-501.16); termómetros; etiquetas con fecha en la comida fría lista para comer que se guarda más de un día (3-501.17); concentración del sanitizante; carne cruda debajo de la comida lista para comer; superficies limpias; plagas; salud e higiene del personal.
Los buenos hábitos diarios hacen fácil cada inspección. Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas.

quiz.q_en: How high off the floor should food be stored?
quiz.q_es: ¿A qué altura del piso se debe guardar la comida?
options_en: On the floor is fine if the box is closed
options_es: En el piso está bien si la caja está cerrada
quiz.why_en: Food is stored at least 6 inches (15 cm) off the floor so it stays protected and the floor can be cleaned (FDA Food Code 3-305.11).
quiz.why_es: La comida se guarda por lo menos a 6 pulgadas (15 cm) del piso para protegerla y poder limpiar el piso (Código de Alimentos de la FDA 3-305.11).

quiz.q_en: Behind a box you find droppings and gnaw marks. What do you do?
quiz.q_es: Detrás de una caja encuentra excremento y marcas de mordidas. ¿Qué hace?
options_en: Spray bug killer behind the shelf
Take a photo and tell your manager right away
Sweep it up and say nothing
Move the box and keep working
options_es: Tomar una foto y avisarle a su gerente de inmediato
Mover la caja y seguir trabajando
quiz.why_en: Pest signs go to the manager right away. Pesticides are a job for the licensed pest control operator: the Food Code allows them only as the label and the law say (7-202.12), and most venues allow no one else.
quiz.why_es: Las señales de plagas se reportan al gerente de inmediato. Los pesticidas son trabajo del técnico autorizado de control de plagas: el Código de Alimentos los permite solo como dicen la etiqueta y la ley (7-202.12), y la mayoría de los lugares de trabajo no deja que nadie más los use.

quiz.q_en: Where do cleaning chemicals go?
quiz.q_es: ¿Dónde se guardan los químicos de limpieza?
options_en: On the shelf above the food
Next to the ice bin so they are easy to grab
On the prep table during service
Below and away from food and anything that touches food
options_es: En el estante encima de la comida
Junto al hielo para tenerlos a la mano
En la mesa de preparación durante el servicio
Debajo y lejos de la comida y de todo lo que toca la comida
quiz.why_en: Chemicals must be kept apart from food and never stored above food or food-contact surfaces, so a drip or spill cannot reach them (7-201.11).
quiz.why_es: Los químicos se guardan aparte de la comida y nunca encima de la comida ni de las superficies que la tocan, para que una gota o un derrame no les caiga (7-201.11).

quiz.q_en: You find a spray bottle with no label. What do you do?
quiz.q_es: Encuentra un atomizador sin etiqueta. ¿Qué hace?
options_en: Don't use it and tell your manager
Smell it to find out what it is
Use it to wipe the tables
Pour it into the sanitizer bucket
options_es: No usarlo y avisarle a su gerente
Echarlo en la cubeta de sanitizante
quiz.why_en: Every working container must be labeled with the chemical's name (7-102.11); if you don't know what it is, don't use it.
quiz.why_es: Todo recipiente de trabajo debe llevar el nombre del químico (7-102.11); si no sabe qué es, no lo use.

quiz.q_en: On a visit, the inspector checks holding temperatures. Which is correct?
quiz.q_es: En una visita, el inspector revisa a qué temperatura se mantiene la comida fría y la caliente. ¿Cuál es la correcta?
options_en: Cold food 50°F or below, hot food 120°F or above
Cold food 32°F or below, hot food 100°F or above
Cold food 41°F or below, hot food 135°F or above
Cold food 45°F or below, hot food 165°F or above
options_es: Comida fría a 50°F o menos, caliente a 120°F o más
Comida fría a 32°F o menos, caliente a 100°F o más
Comida fría a 41°F o menos, caliente a 135°F o más
Comida fría a 45°F o menos, caliente a 165°F o más
quiz.why_en: The Food Code holds cold food at 41°F (5°C) or below and hot food at 135°F (57°C) or above (3-501.16).
quiz.why_es: El Código de Alimentos pide mantener la comida fría a 41°F (5°C) o menos y la caliente a 135°F (57°C) o más (3-501.16).

facts.claim: The premises must be kept free of insects, rodents and other pests, and the operation must routinely inspect incoming deliveries and the premises for evidence of pests and eliminate harborage conditions.
Outer openings (doors, windows, gaps) must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents, e.g. doors kept closed and openings sealed.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 6-202.15 Outer Openings, Protected

facts.claim: Inside, refuse receptacles that hold food residue are kept covered when not in continuous use and after they are filled; outside receptacles have tight-fitting lids or doors (5-501.113). Refuse is removed often enough to prevent odors and pest attraction (5-502.11).
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 5-501.113 Covering Receptacles; 5-502.11 Frequency of Removal

facts.claim: Food must be stored in a clean, dry location where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination, at least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.
Food that is unsafe, adulterated or contaminated (such as food pests have gotten into) must be discarded.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-701.11 Discarding or Reconditioning Unsafe, Adulterated, or Contaminated Food

facts.claim: Poisonous or toxic materials, including pesticides, must be used according to law and the manufacturer's label; a restricted-use pesticide may be applied only by a certified applicator or a person under their direct supervision. Many venues allow only the licensed pest control operator to apply any pesticide — your local rules or your venue may be stricter.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 7-202.12 Conditions of Use

facts.claim: Poisonous or toxic materials must be separated from food by spacing or partitioning and must not be stored above food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service and single-use articles.
Working containers of cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies must be clearly and individually labeled with the common name of the material.
Employers must keep Safety Data Sheets for hazardous chemicals readily accessible to employees during each work shift.

A handwashing sink must be accessible at all times and used for no purpose other than handwashing, and it must be supplied with hand cleanser and a hand-drying provision: individual disposable towels, a continuous towel system, a heated-air hand dryer or an air-knife hand dryer.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink; 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser; 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision

facts.claim: Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held cold at 5°C (41°F) or less, or hot at 57°C (135°F) or above.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-501.16 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding

facts.claim: Food temperature measuring devices must be provided and readily accessible, and cold and hot holding units must have a temperature measuring device.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices; 4-204.112 Temperature Measuring Devices

facts.claim: Refrigerated ready-to-eat TCS food prepared on site, or opened from a commercial package, and held more than 24 hours must be date marked (no more than 7 days at 41°F or below, counting the day of preparation or opening as day 1).
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-501.17 Ready-to-Eat, TCS Food, Date Marking

facts.claim: Chemical sanitizer must be used at the concentration the label and the Code specify, a test kit must be provided to measure sanitizer concentration, and wiping cloths are held in sanitizer at that concentration.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 4-501.114 Chemical Sanitization; 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices; 3-304.14 Wiping Cloths

facts.claim: Raw animal foods must be separated from ready-to-eat foods during storage, for example by storing raw meat below ready-to-eat food, and food is protected from cross-contamination by storing it in packages, covered containers or wrappings.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-302.11 Packaged and Unpackaged Food — Separation, Packaging, and Segregation

facts.claim: Food-contact surfaces must be cleaned at the frequency the Code requires (at least every 4 hours when in constant use with TCS food).
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 4-602.11 Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils

facts.claim: Food employees must keep hands clean, wear hair restraints (hats, hair coverings or nets), eat and drink only in designated areas away from exposed food, and report certain illnesses and symptoms to the person in charge.
facts.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 2-301.11 Clean Condition; 2-402.11 Effectiveness (Hair Restraints); 2-401.11 Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco; 2-201.11 Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person in Charge, and Conditional Employees

issues.where: beat 7 say_en / say_es / onscreen_en / onscreen_es; keypoints_en[5] / keypoints_es[5]
issues.problem: The sick-worker rule is too weak. 'You should not work with food while you are sick' makes it sound like advice and like the person can still come in and do other work. Under the Food Code, a food employee with vomiting or diarrhea is EXCLUDED, which means they may not work in the food establishment at all, not just kept away from food. The line also says to report only 'before your shift', but symptoms that start during the shift must be reported right away too.
issues.correct: EN say: "And if you have vomiting or diarrhea, tell your manager before your shift, or right away if it starts at work. With vomiting or diarrhea, you must not work." (about +6 words, total stays near 409). ES say: "Y si tiene vómito o diarrea, avísele a su gerente antes del turno, o de inmediato si le empieza en el trabajo. Con vómito o diarrea, usted no puede trabajar." On-screen EN: 'Vomiting or diarrhea? Tell your manager. Do not work.' ES: '¿Vómito o diarrea? Avísele a su gerente. No trabaje.' Keypoint EN: '...tell your manager before your shift, or right away at work, if you have vomiting or diarrhea; you must not work while you have them.' Change the ES keypoint to match.
issues.source: 2022 FDA Food Code 2-201.11(A) (employees must report symptoms to the person in charge), 2-201.12(A)(1) (exclude a food employee who has vomiting or diarrhea), 1-201.10(B) definition of 'Exclude' (prevent a person from working as an employee in a food establishment or entering it as an employee)

issues.problem: 'Germs, chemicals, or objects in food can cause it' says objects cause foodborne ILLNESS. Physical objects such as glass or metal cause injuries like cuts, broken teeth or choking. They do not cause illness. The illness itself comes from germs (and their toxins) or chemicals. The lesson separates physical hazards correctly in beat 6, so beat 2 contradicts it.
issues.correct: EN: "Germs or chemicals in food can cause it. And objects in food, like glass, can hurt people too." ES: "La pueden causar gérmenes o químicos en la comida. Y los objetos en la comida, como un vidrio, también pueden lastimar a la gente."
issues.source: CDC, Foodborne Illnesses and Germs (illness is caused by germs/toxins or chemicals in food); 2022 FDA Food Code 1-201.10(B) definition of 'Hazard' (biological, chemical, or physical property that may cause an unacceptable consumer health risk). Physical hazards cause injury: Food Code Annex 4 (HACCP, physical hazards)

issues.problem: The citation is wrong. The definition of 'hazard' in 1-201.10 only says a hazard is a biological, chemical, or physical property. It does not list glass, metal, hair or bandages as examples, yet the explanation cites it as if it did.
issues.correct: EN: "Objects like glass, metal, hair, or a bandage are physical hazards; the Food Code defines a hazard as biological, chemical, or physical (1-201.10)." ES: "Los objetos como vidrio, metal, pelo o una curita son peligros físicos; el Código de Alimentos define un peligro como biológico, químico o físico (1-201.10)."
issues.source: 2022 FDA Food Code 1-201.10(B), definition of 'Hazard'

issues.correct: onscreen_es: '(poco cocido)'. say_es: 'Uno: comida mantenida a una temperatura incorrecta.' keypoints_es: 'temperatura incorrecta al mantener la comida (fría o caliente), cocción insuficiente, ...'
issues.source: English beat 5 text ('not cooked enough', 'food held at the wrong temperature'); 2022 FDA Food Code 3-501.16 (hot and cold holding)

issues.source: English beat 1 on-screen text ('away from the hot holding unit')

issues.problem: The Spanish explanation leaves out what the risk is about ('for food poisoning'), so 'como de mayor riesgo' is left hanging and does not match the English.
issues.correct: 'Los CDC señalan a las personas embarazadas, los niños pequeños, los adultos mayores y las personas con el sistema inmunitario débil como las que tienen mayor riesgo de enfermarse por alimentos.'

issues.where: Beat 9 say_en / say_es ("Your supervisor decides if you stay home or do other work") + facts claim for 2-201.12 + quiz Q5 why_en / why_es ("who decides if you stay home")
issues.problem: It sounds like the supervisor chooses freely. Under the Food Code, the person in charge MUST exclude or restrict by fixed criteria. An employee with vomiting or diarrhea (from an infectious cause) must be excluded, which means staying out of work. "Do other work" is not an option for those symptoms. Workers may think they can stay on with diarrhea if the supervisor agrees.
issues.correct: say_en: "With vomiting or diarrhea, you must stay home. For anything else, your supervisor follows the rules: home, or other work." say_es: "Si tiene vómito o diarrea, debe quedarse en casa. En los demás casos, su supervisor sigue las reglas: a casa o a otro trabajo." Facts: "The person in charge must exclude or restrict a food employee as 2-201.12 requires (vomiting or diarrhea = exclude); 2-201.13 sets when they may come back (for example, 24 hours with no symptoms, or a doctor's note, unless they have a Big 6 diagnosis)." Q5 why_en: "…you must report it to the person in charge (2-201.11), who must then exclude or restrict you under the Food Code rules (2-201.12)." Q5 why_es: "…debe reportarlo a la persona a cargo (2-201.11), que debe sacarlo del trabajo o limitar sus tareas según las reglas del Código (2-201.12)."
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 2-201.12(A) ('Except when the symptom is from a noninfectious condition, EXCLUDE a FOOD EMPLOYEE if the FOOD EMPLOYEE is (1) Symptomatic with vomiting or diarrhea…') and 2-201.13(A)(1) (reinstate after at least 24 h without symptoms or with medical documentation, except for listed diagnoses); NM 2019 Retail Food Field Guide, Employee Health §2-2 https://www.env.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2018/05/Employee-Health-Section-2-2-2019-Retail-and-Manufactured-Food-Field-Guide-Final-12.7.18.pdf; NACCHO CIFOR Tool 7A https://cifor.naccho.org/uploads/resources/Tool-7A-Employee-Illness-Decision-Guide.pdf

issues.where: Beat 2 say_en / say_es / onscreen (the 'When to wash' list), keypoint 1 EN / ES
issues.problem: The list leaves out the main trigger in 2-301.14: wash immediately before you start food prep, including at the start of the shift and when you come back to the line. The section cited lists every other trigger, so a worker could think washing is only needed after something dirty.
issues.correct: Add it first. EN: "When do you wash? Before you start food prep. After the restroom. …" ES: "¿Cuándo debe lavarse las manos? Antes de empezar a preparar comida. Después de ir al baño. …" Add a first icon, 'start of work / before food prep' ('al empezar / antes de preparar comida'). Keypoint 1 should start with: "Wash your hands right before you start working with food, after the restroom, …" / "Lávese las manos justo antes de empezar a trabajar con comida, después de ir al baño, …"
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 2-301.14 ('…shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms … immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A)…(I)')

issues.where: Beat 6 say_en / say_es / onscreen, keypoint 6 EN / ES, objective 4
issues.problem: The glove-change triggers leave out one that the code names: an interruption in the operation. Taking cash, answering the phone or stepping away from the line are interruptions. At a concession stand, gloves worn while handling money and then food is a common violation. The facts list includes it, but the script does not.
issues.correct: say_en: "Change them when they tear, get dirty, after any interruption like taking cash, or when you switch tasks…" say_es: "Cámbielos cuando se rompan, cuando se ensucien, después de cualquier interrupción, como cobrar, o cuando cambie de tarea…" Add a fourth red flag on screen: a gloved hand takes cash, then reaches for a bun. Keypoint 6: "…change them when they tear, get dirty, after an interruption (like handling money), or when you switch tasks (3-304.15)." / "…cámbielos cuando se rompan, se ensucien, después de una interrupción (como cobrar) o cuando cambie de tarea (3-304.15)."
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-304.15(A) ('…discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation'); text reproduced in Minnesota Rule 4626.0287 https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4626.0287/version/2019-01-02T09:58:14-06:00 and Oregon Food Code Fact Sheet 10 https://oregon.gov/oda/Documents/Publications/FoodSafety/FoodCodeGlovesFactSheet10.pdf

issues.where: Beat 11 onscreen caption ('2-201.11 — cuts on the hands: cover + glove'), keypoint 10, facts claim citing 2-201.11(A)(1)(e)(i)
issues.problem: The citation does not match the rule. 2-201.11(A)(1)(e) is about a lesion containing PUS (a boil or an infected wound that is open or draining). On the hands or wrists, it must be reported UNLESS it has an impermeable cover such as a finger cot or stall with a single-use glove over it. It is not a rule about any small cut. The facts line ('A lesion on the hands or wrists must be protected…') drops the 'containing pus' condition.
issues.correct: Caption EN: "Cuts on the hands: cover + glove. An infected cut with pus: also tell your supervisor (2-201.11)." Caption ES: "Heridas en las manos: cubrir + guante. Herida infectada con pus: avise también a su supervisor (2-201.11)." Facts: "A lesion containing pus (boil or infected wound, open or draining) on the hands or wrists must be reported unless it is protected by an impermeable cover such as a finger cot or stall with a single-use glove worn over it." Covering a plain cut with a waterproof bandage and a glove is still good practice. Keep the spoken line and keep 'your local rules or your venue may be stricter'.

issues.where: Beat 8 on-screen caption ('max 4 hours — Food Code 3-501.19'); keypoint 7
issues.problem: 'Max 4 hours' is stated as the Food Code limit, but 3-501.19 has two options. Paragraph (B) is the 4-hour option. Paragraph (C) allows up to 6 hours for cold food: it must start at 41°F or below, must never go above 70°F, and must be monitored and marked. The lesson teaches only the 4-hour option, so calling 4 hours the maximum is misleading.

issues.where: Beat 3 (say_en, onscreen_en, say_es, onscreen_es); objectives_en[0] / objectives_es[0]; keypoints_en[1] / keypoints_es[1]
issues.problem: "Anything stuffed, like stuffed peppers" (ES: "cualquier comida rellena, como chiles rellenos") is too broad. The Food Code's 165°F rule covers stuffed fish, meat, pasta, poultry and ratites, plus any stuffing that contains fish, meat, poultry or ratites. A pepper or chile relleno filled only with cheese, rice or vegetables is a plant food: 3-401.13 says 135°F for hot holding. The Spanish example makes this worse, because chiles rellenos are usually filled with cheese. "Stuffed foods" in the objective and key point has the same problem.
issues.correct: say_en: "Chicken, turkey, stuffed pasta, and anything stuffed with meat, fish or poultry, like peppers stuffed with ground beef: 165 degrees. The moment it reaches 165, it is safe." (+7 words, which brings the lesson to 417). On-screen icons: chicken, turkey, a pepper stuffed with ground beef, stuffed pasta. say_es: "Pollo, pavo, pasta rellena y cualquier comida rellena con carne, pescado o pollo, como chiles rellenos de carne molida: 165 grados. En cuanto llega a 165, ya es segura." Key point: "165°F (less than 1 second): chicken, turkey and other poultry, stuffed pasta, and any food stuffed with meat, fish or poultry." ES: "165 °F (menos de 1 segundo): pollo, pavo y otras aves, pasta rellena y cualquier comida rellena con carne, pescado o aves." Objective: change "stuffed foods" to "stuffed pasta and foods stuffed with meat, fish or poultry" (ES: "pasta rellena y comidas rellenas con carne, pescado o aves").
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §3-401.11(A)(3): 165°F (<1 s) for poultry, stuffed fish/meat/pasta/poultry/ratites, or stuffing containing fish, meat, poultry or ratites; §3-401.13: plant foods cooked for hot holding, 135°F. State adoptions: https://regulations.vlex.com/vid/s-c-code-regs-959385296 , https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title2/agency5/chapter585/section720/

issues.where: Beat 5 / Beat 4 (say_en, say_es); keypoints_en[3] / keypoints_es[3]; objectives ("eggs")
issues.problem: The lesson only teaches eggs at 145°F for 15 seconds, which is the rule for eggs cracked for a customer's order. It never says that raw eggs cooked ahead for hot holding must reach 155°F for 17 seconds. Examples are a pan of scrambled eggs for a steam table or breakfast-burrito filling. A learner would reasonably apply 145°F to batch eggs and undercook them.
issues.correct: Add eggs to the 155°F beat. Beat 4 say_en: "Burgers and other ground meat, ground fish, injected meat, and eggs cooked ahead to hold hot: 155 degrees for 17 seconds." (+3 words; with the stuffed fix the total is 420. If needed, drop "And remember," in beat 6 to stay under the limit.) Add a pan of scrambled eggs in a steam table to the beat 4 card. say_es: "Hamburguesas y otras carnes molidas, pescado molido, carne inyectada y huevos que se cocinan antes para mantenerlos calientes: 155 grados durante 17 segundos." Key point 3 EN: add "and eggs cooked ahead for hot holding" / ES: "y huevos que se cocinan antes para mantenerlos calientes".
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §3-401.11(A)(2)(c): raw eggs not prepared as in (A)(1)(a) [broken to order for immediate service], 155°F for 17 s. FDA: https://www.fda.gov/food/training-resources/assuring-safety-eggs-and-menu-and-deli-items-made-raw-shell-eggs ; state text: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincode/title02/agency5/chapter585/section700/

issues.problem: The 2-hour limit on reheating is cited to §3-403.11(A) and (E). Paragraph (E) is about reheating leftover unsliced meat roasts with the roast oven parameters. The 2-hour rule is paragraph (D).
issues.correct: source: "FDA Food Code 2022, §3-403.11(A) and (D)"
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §3-403.11(D): "Reheating for hot holding as specified under ¶¶ (A)-(C) shall be done rapidly and the time the FOOD is between 5°C (41°F) and the temperatures specified ... may not exceed 2 hours"; (E) = unsliced roasts. Adopted text: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-3-403.11

issues.problem: The word order is ambiguous. "Recalentar la comida que se mantendrá caliente a 165 °F..." and "Recaliente la comida cocinada y enfriada que se mantendrá caliente a 165 °F..." read naturally as "the food that will be held hot AT 165°F". That is not the English meaning: reheat TO 165°F, then hold at 135°F.
issues.correct: objectives_es[4]: "Recalentar a 165 °F durante 15 segundos, en 2 horas o menos, la comida que se va a mantener caliente." keypoints_es[6]: "Recaliente a 165 °F durante 15 segundos, en 2 horas o menos, la comida cocinada y enfriada que se va a mantener caliente; después manténgala a 135 °F o más."
issues.source: Matches objectives_en[4] / keypoints_en[6] and FDA Food Code 2022 §3-403.11(A),(D); §3-501.16(A)(1)

issues.problem: "Llévela ahí rápido, en 2 horas o menos" copies the English idiom "get it there" word for word. In Spanish, "ahí" points to a place, not to a temperature, so the line is unnatural and unclear.
issues.correct: "Hágalo rápido: debe llegar a 165 grados en 2 horas o menos."
issues.source: Same meaning as say_en beat 9; FDA Food Code 2022 §3-403.11(D)

issues.problem: "torta de hamburguesa" is confusing for Latin-American staff. In Mexico a "torta" is a sandwich, and in much of the region it means a cake. A patty is normally "carne de hamburguesa".
issues.correct: "Tarjeta: '155 °F · 17 segundos' con íconos: carne de hamburguesa, pescado molido, una jeringa de marinada sobre un trozo de carne. Pie: '3-401.11'."
issues.source: Natural LatAm kitchen usage; matches onscreen_en "burger patty"

issues.problem: "Descongelar la comida con una de las cuatro formas seguras" uses the wrong preposition. The natural phrasing is "de una de las formas".
issues.correct: "Descongelar la comida de una de las cuatro formas seguras."
issues.source: Spanish usage ("de una forma / de esta manera"); matches objectives_en[5]

issues.where: Beat 9 (say_en / say_es, onscreen small text 'signs can start within minutes'), keypoints and the last 'facts' entry
issues.problem: The lesson says only that a reaction 'can start within minutes'. FDA says symptoms can show up anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours after eating. Staff could brush off a customer who starts feeling bad 30–60 minutes after their meal.
issues.correct: EN: "It can start within minutes, or up to a couple of hours after eating." ES: "Puede empezar en minutos o hasta un par de horas después de comer." Onscreen: "Signs can start within minutes or hours" / "Las señales pueden empezar en minutos o en horas". Make the same change in the facts entry.
issues.source: U.S. FDA, 'Food Allergies: What You Need to Know' (fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/food-allergies-what-you-need-know): symptoms may appear within a few minutes to a few hours.

issues.where: Beat 9 (say_en / say_es, red banner) and keypoint 9 (EN + ES)
issues.problem: The course is for stadium and large-venue staff. Many of these venues have their own emergency number or on-site medical team, and that is often the faster way to get help. The lesson only says 'Call 911', so a worker may not know to use the venue's emergency line.
issues.correct: EN: "Call 911 or your venue's emergency number right away, tell your manager, and stay with the person." ES: "Llame de inmediato al 911 o al número de emergencias de su lugar de trabajo, avísele a su gerente y quédese con la persona." Banner: "CALL 911 / VENUE EMERGENCY NOW". This adds 4 words, so the total goes from 410 to 414 and is still within 320–420.
issues.source: Course rule: 'your local rules or your venue may be stricter'. This is a venue procedure point, not a Food Code requirement.

issues.problem: The entry says whole (intact) cuts of meat cook to 145°F for 15 seconds. That is not true for whole roasts. Under 3-401.11(B), beef, pork, lamb and ham roasts follow a time and temperature table (for example 145°F for 4 minutes; oven-temperature limits also apply). The on-screen line 'whole cuts … cook to 145°F' is still fine for the shelf order.
issues.correct: "Fish and intact meat (steaks, chops) 145°F for 15 seconds (whole roasts: the time and temperature table in 3-401.11(B), e.g. 145°F for 4 minutes); ground (comminuted) meat and fish 155°F for 17 seconds; poultry 165°F for <1 second."
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-401.11(A)(1)(b), (A)(2), (A)(3) and (B) Raw Animal Foods / whole meat roasts

issues.problem: Both cited sections are about the person in charge: their allergen knowledge (2-102.11(C)) and their duty to train staff in allergy awareness (2-103.11(N)). The 2022 Food Code section that deals most directly with telling customers about allergens in unpackaged food is not cited.
issues.correct: Add 3-602.12(C) to the caption: "FDA Food Code 2-102.11 · 2-103.11 · 3-602.12(C)". ES: "Código de Alimentos de la FDA 2-102.11 · 2-103.11 · 3-602.12(C)".
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 Summary of Changes: 3-602.12(C) added, written notification to consumers of major food allergens as ingredients in unpackaged food (also in the Pennsylvania Dept. of Agriculture notice on the 2022 Food Code changes)

issues.where: beat 3 (say_en, say_es, onscreen_en/es checklist line '✓ After each use'), keypoints_en[1] / keypoints_es[1], quiz[0].why_en / why_es
issues.problem: 'Clean and sanitize every surface that touches food after each use' is cited to 4-602.11, but 4-602.11(A) has no 'after each use' rule. It is a training habit, not Food Code text. The quiz explanation repeats it as an FDA rule. The real 4-602.11(A)(1) trigger, a switch between different raw animal foods (raw beef to raw chicken), is missing from the lesson.
issues.correct: Replace the 'after each use' line with the Code trigger. say_en: 'When? Clean and sanitize surfaces that touch food when you switch from one raw meat to another, like raw beef to raw chicken. When you switch from raw meat to ready-to-eat food. When you get interrupted and germs may have gotten on it. And if it's used all day with foods that need temperature control, at least every four hours.' Onscreen: '✓ Raw meat → a different raw meat (🥩 → 🍗)'. say_es: '¿Cuándo? Limpie y desinfecte las superficies que tocan la comida cuando cambie de una carne cruda a otra, por ejemplo de res cruda a pollo crudo. Cuando pase de carne cruda a comida lista para comer. Cuando lo interrumpan y se haya podido contaminar. Y si la usa todo el día con alimentos que necesitan control de temperatura, por lo menos cada cuatro horas.' Keypoint: '...when you switch between different raw animal foods, when you switch from raw to ready-to-eat food, between raw produce and TCS food, any time contamination may have happened, and at least every 4 hours when in constant use with TCS food (4-602.11).' Quiz 1 why_en: '...at least every 4 hours (4-602.11(C)), and also when you switch foods or when it may have been contaminated.' If 'after each use' stays as a venue habit, drop the 4-602.11 citation for it.
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §4-602.11(A)(1)–(5) and (C); §4-702.11 (sanitize after cleaning, before use)

issues.where: beat 6 (say_en/say_es, onscreen chlorine card), keypoints_en[4] / keypoints_es[4], facts (4-501.114)
issues.problem: 'Chlorine: 50 to 100 ppm. The right number depends on the water temperature and pH,' cited to 4-501.114, gets the rule backwards and incomplete. The 4-501.114(A) table sets the MINIMUM WATER TEMPERATURE for each concentration and pH: 25–49 ppm needs 120°F, 50–99 ppm needs 100°F (pH ≤10) or 75°F (pH ≤8), 100 ppm needs 55°F. The 50–100 ppm range is a common target, not the Code's only allowed range, and the EPA product label governs.
issues.correct: say_en: 'Chlorine: usually 50 to 100 parts per million. Follow the product label, and use water warm enough for that strength.' Onscreen note: 'follow the label · water temperature and pH matter'. Keypoint: 'chlorine: follow the label, usually 50–100 ppm; the water must be at least the temperature the Food Code table sets for that strength and pH (4-501.114(A))'. say_es: 'Cloro: normalmente de 50 a 100 partes por millón. Siga la etiqueta del producto y use agua lo bastante tibia para esa concentración.' Quiz 4 can keep 50–100 ppm as the answer (the other options are clearly wrong).
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §4-501.114 (A) chlorine table, opening paragraph (EPA-registered label use instructions); §7-204.11

issues.problem: English 'When you get interrupted and the surface may be dirty' does not match the Spanish 'se haya podido contaminar', and it is weaker than the Code wording (any time contamination may have occurred; germs are invisible, so 'dirty' misleads).
issues.correct: say_en: 'When you get interrupted and germs may have gotten on it.' (matches keypoints_en[1] 'may have contaminated them' and the Spanish)
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §4-602.11(A)(5)

issues.problem: 'Change the wash, rinse and sanitizer water when it gets dirty or cools down (4-501.18)': 4-501.18 only says the solutions must be kept clean. The 'cools down' part comes from the temperature rules.
issues.correct: 'Keep the wash, rinse and sanitizer water clean: change it when it gets dirty (4-501.18). Change the wash water when it drops below 110°F (4-501.19).' ES: 'Mantenga limpia el agua de lavado, de enjuague y el desinfectante: cámbiela cuando esté sucia (4-501.18). Cambie el agua de lavado cuando baje de 110°F (4-501.19).'

issues.where: facts[] item for wiping cloths (source field)
issues.problem: Wrong paragraph letters. 'Free of food debris and visible soil' is 3-304.14(D), 'stored off the floor' is (E). Paragraph (F) is single-use disposable sanitizer wipes.
issues.correct: source: 'FDA Food Code 2022, 3-304.14(B), (D), (E)'
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §3-304.14 (text reproduced in Minnesota Rule 4626.0285: https://revisor.mn.gov/rules/pdf/4626.0285/2019-01-02%2009:58:13+00:00; Massachusetts guidance: https://www.westboylston-ma.gov/sites/g/files/vyhlif1421/f/uploads/wiping-cloths-in-food-service-nov-2018.pdf)

issues.problem: The stem 'must be at least…' leaves out the Code's detergent-label alternative, so the marked answer is not strictly always true. The explanation's 'hand-washing water for dishes' is easy to confuse with the handwashing-sink rule (100°F, 5-202.12). The Spanish 'trastes' is regional (Mexico / Central America).
issues.correct: q_en: 'Unless the detergent label says otherwise, the wash water in the first compartment must be at least…' q_es: 'Salvo que la etiqueta del detergente diga otra cosa, el agua de lavado del primer compartimento debe estar por lo menos a…' why_en: 'The FDA Food Code (4-501.19) says the wash water in a sink for washing dishes by hand must be 110°F or hotter, or the temperature on the detergent label, so change it when it cools down.' why_es: 'El Código de Alimentos de la FDA (4-501.19) pide que el agua del fregadero para lavar platos y utensilios a mano esté a 110°F o más (o a la temperatura de la etiqueta del detergente), así que cámbiela cuando se enfríe.'
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022 §4-501.19; §5-202.12 (handwashing sink 100°F)

issues.problem: 'Cuaternario de amonio' has the words in the wrong order. The usual Spanish term is 'amonio cuaternario' (compuestos de amonio cuaternario).
issues.correct: onscreen_es: 'AMONIO CUATERNARIO ("quat"): "siga la etiqueta"'; say_es: 'Amonio cuaternario, o "quat": siga la etiqueta del producto.'; keypoints_es[4]: '...amonio cuaternario ("quat") según la etiqueta del fabricante...'
issues.source: Standard Spanish chemical name (compuestos de amonio cuaternario)

issues.problem: 'En la bolsa del delantal': 'bolsa' means pocket only in Mexico. Elsewhere it reads as 'bag'.
issues.correct: 'En el bolsillo del delantal'
issues.source: Latin-American Spanish usage (bolsillo = pocket)

issues.problem: 'Raspe la comida a la basura' is unnatural.
issues.correct: 'Paso uno: raspe los restos de comida en la basura.'
issues.source: Natural Spanish phrasing; FDA Food Code 2022 §4-603.12 (scrape food debris over a garbage receptacle)

issues.problem: 'Deje las piezas en el desinfectante': 'piezas' is vague and unnatural for dishes and utensils.
issues.correct: 'Deje los platos y utensilios en el desinfectante el tiempo que indica la etiqueta.'
issues.source: Natural Latin-American Spanish

issues.problem: The on-screen text 'Las reglas locales o su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictos' differs from the spoken line ('Las reglas de su localidad o de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas'), and the agreement reads awkwardly.
issues.correct: onscreen_es: 'Las reglas de su localidad o de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas.' (same as the spoken line)
issues.source: Consistency with say_es; Spanish agreement

issues.problem: 'Revíselo.' for 'Test it.' is unclear: 'lo' has no clear referent. 'Lo único que debe recordar' means 'the only thing you need to remember', not 'the one thing to remember'.
issues.correct: onscreen_es: 'Primero limpie. Después desinfecte. Mídalo con la tira.' say_es: 'Lo más importante que debe recordar: primero limpie, después desinfecte, y mida la concentración con una tira de prueba. ...'
issues.source: Natural Latin-American Spanish

issues.problem: 'Cuando ... la tira de prueba salga baja' is awkward; it is the solution's strength that reads low.
issues.correct: '...y cambie la solución cuando esté sucia o cuando la tira de prueba marque poca concentración.'
issues.source: Natural Latin-American Spanish

issues.where: Beat 8 onscreen_es (label on the rice container)
issues.problem: 'Usar antes del DOM' means 'use BEFORE Sunday', which makes Saturday the last day. That contradicts the English 'Use by SUN', the calendar's 'Día 7 — último día' (Sunday) and the date-marking rule.
issues.correct: 'ARROZ COCIDO · Preparado LUN · Usar hasta el DOM' (or 'Último día: DOM').
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-501.17(A): date-marked for a maximum of 7 days, and the day of preparation is Day 1. Mon = Day 1, so Sun = Day 7 is still a usable day.

issues.where: Beat 8 say_en / say_es, keypoint 8 (EN + ES), objective 4
issues.problem: Date marking is taught only for food 'you make here'. 3-501.17(B) also covers commercially processed ready-to-eat TCS food once its package is opened and held more than 24 hours, such as opened deli meat (which beat 3 already names). Staff will think opened packages need no date.
issues.correct: EN: 'Ready-to-eat TCS food you make here or open from a package, and keep more than 24 hours, like cooked rice, cut melon or opened deli meat, needs a date. At 41°F or below, you have 7 days at most, and the day you make it or open it is day 1.' (about 415 words in total, still ≤420). ES: 'Los alimentos TCS listos para comer que usted prepara aquí o que saca de un paquete que abre, y guarda más de 24 horas, como arroz cocido, melón cortado o carnes frías abiertas, necesitan fecha. A 41°F o menos, tiene un máximo de 7 días, y el día en que lo prepara o lo abre cuenta como el día 1.' Keypoint 8 should add: 'opened packages too; the day you open it is day 1, and never past the maker's use-by date.'
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-501.17(B): the day the original container is opened counts as Day 1, and the date may not exceed a manufacturer's use-by date based on food safety. 3-501.18(A) also applies to food under 3-501.17(B).

issues.where: Beat 6 say_en / say_es ('Never leave boxes on the floor')
issues.problem: 'Never' is stricter than the Code, and bar and stand staff will meet the exceptions. 3-305.11 lets pressurized beverage containers (kegs), cased food in waterproof containers (canned or bottled drinks) and milk in plastic crates sit on a clean, dry floor. Packaged food may also sit lower than 6 inches on case-lot equipment such as dollies or pallets.
issues.correct: Say 'Keep food boxes off the floor: store food at least 6 inches off the floor, on a shelf or rack.' Add a keypoint: 'Exceptions: kegs, cases of canned or bottled drinks and milk in plastic crates may sit on a clean, dry floor; dollies and pallets are allowed. Your local rules or your venue may be stricter.' (ES to match.)
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-305.11(A)(3), (B) and (C); 4-204.122 (case lot handling equipment).

issues.problem: The footnote 'TCS = needs time and temperature control for safety · 3-202.11' presents 3-202.11 as the source of the TCS definition. 3-202.11 is the receiving-temperature rule. The definition is in 1-201.10(B).
issues.correct: Put '· 3-202.11' on the big text ('Cold TCS food: 41°F or below · 3-202.11'). Make the footnote 'TCS = needs time and temperature control for safety' (optionally '· 1-201.10'). Same change in ES.
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 1-201.10(B) (definition of 'Time/temperature control for safety food'); 3-202.11(A).

issues.problem: 'Fiambres' is mainly Southern Cone and Spain usage. Many Latin-American (Mexican, Central American, Caribbean) kitchen workers say 'carnes frías', and 'fiambres' may not be understood.
issues.correct: 'como el pollo crudo, las carnes frías o el melón cortado'
issues.source: Latin-American Spanish usage (course rule: natural Latin-American Spanish, low reading level).

issues.where: Beat 5 say_es and keypoint 4 ES ('sellos abiertos')
issues.problem: The English says 'broken seals'. 'Sellos abiertos' (opened seals) is weaker and less natural for a damaged package.
issues.correct: 'sellos rotos' (e.g. 'bolsas rotas y sellos rotos', or 'bolsas rotas y empaques con el sello roto').
issues.source: Match to the English text; FDA Food Code 2022, 3-202.15 (package integrity).

issues.problem: The keypoint cites only 3-202.15 (package integrity) for rejecting pests, off smells and slime. Those rejections rest on food being safe and unadulterated (3-101.11), as the draft's own fact list says.
issues.correct: Cite '(3-202.15, 3-101.11)' in both languages.
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-101.11 (Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented); 3-202.15.

issues.problem: 'Got warm on the way' / 'se calentó en el camino' claims the thawing happened during this delivery. The signs only show that the food thawed and refroze at some point before it reached the stand (previous temperature abuse). The explanation also has no section number, unlike the others.
issues.correct: EN: 'Frozen food must arrive frozen solid; large ice crystals and frozen liquid show it thawed and was frozen again before it reached you (FDA Food Code 3-202.11).' ES: 'La comida congelada debe llegar bien dura; los cristales grandes y el líquido congelado muestran que se descongeló y se volvió a congelar antes de llegar a usted (Código de Alimentos de la FDA 3-202.11).'
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-202.11(E) and (F) (received frozen; free of evidence of previous temperature abuse).

issues.problem: The lesson cites 7-202.12 for "Only the licensed pest control operator applies pesticides." 7-202.12 does not say that. It says (A) pesticides must be used as the law, this Code and the manufacturer's label allow (the label must allow use in a food establishment), and applied so nothing gets contaminated. Only (B) limits RESTRICTED-USE pesticides to a certified applicator or someone under that person's direct supervision. "Only the pest control operator" is a venue rule that is stricter than the Code, not a Food Code rule. Your own facts list says this correctly; the lesson text does not.
issues.correct: keypoints_en[2]: "See a pest sign? Take a photo and tell your manager right away. Throw away food that pests got into (3-701.11). Leave pesticides to the licensed pest control operator. The Food Code allows pesticides only as the label and the law say, and restricted-use pesticides only by a certified applicator (7-202.12). Your local rules or your venue may be stricter." keypoints_es[2]: "¿Ve una señal de plagas? Tome una foto y avísele a su gerente de inmediato. Bote la comida en la que se metieron las plagas (3-701.11). Deje los pesticidas en manos del técnico autorizado de control de plagas. El Código de Alimentos permite usar pesticidas solo como dicen la etiqueta y la ley, y los pesticidas de uso restringido solo los aplica un aplicador certificado (7-202.12). Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas." quiz[1].why_en: "Pest signs go to the manager right away. Pesticides are a job for the licensed pest control operator: the Food Code allows them only as the label and the law say (7-202.12), and most venues allow no one else." quiz[1].why_es: "Las señales de plagas se reportan al gerente de inmediato. Los pesticidas son trabajo del técnico autorizado de control de plagas: el Código de Alimentos los permite solo como dicen la etiqueta y la ley (7-202.12), y la mayoría de los lugares de trabajo no deja que nadie más los use."
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 7-202.12 Conditions of Use (A)(1)(a)–(d), (A)(2), (B); restricted-use certified applicator as defined in 7 USC 136(e) (FIFRA). The same text is adopted in Minn. R. 4626.1610.

issues.problem: "Never spray bug killer yourself. Only the licensed pest control operator applies pesticides" is presented as a general rule. It is a venue policy that is stricter than the Code. The course rule says to add "your local rules or your venue may be stricter" when that is the case, and beat 4 does not.
issues.correct: say_en: "See a sign of pests? Take a photo and tell your manager right away. Food that pests got into goes in the trash. And never spray bug killer yourself. Pesticides are a job for the licensed pest control operator. Your local rules or your venue may be stricter." (about +8 words; total stays ≤ 420). say_es: "¿Ve una señal de plagas? Tome una foto y avísele a su gerente de inmediato. La comida en la que se metieron las plagas va a la basura. Y nunca use insecticida por su cuenta. Los pesticidas son trabajo del técnico autorizado de control de plagas. Las reglas locales o las de su lugar de trabajo pueden ser más estrictas."
issues.source: Course hard rule ("When a US state or the venue may be stricter, say 'your local rules or your venue may be stricter'"); FDA Food Code 2022, 7-202.12

issues.problem: "Refuse receptacles must be covered" overstates the Code. Inside the establishment, receptacles must be covered when they hold food residue and are not in continuous use, and after they are filled. Outside, they need tight-fitting lids or doors. Telling staff to "keep the lids on" is fine, because it is stricter than the Code, but the facts sheet misstates the rule.
issues.correct: "Inside, refuse receptacles that hold food residue are kept covered when not in continuous use and after they are filled; outside receptacles have tight-fitting lids or doors (5-501.113). Refuse is removed often enough to prevent odors and pest attraction (5-502.11)."
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 5-501.113 Covering Receptacles (A)(1)–(2), (B); 5-502.11 Frequency of Removal

issues.problem: The whole pest-prevention list carries one citation, 3-305.11. That section only covers storage in a clean, dry place at least 6 in (15 cm) off the floor. Doors and gaps, trash, covered food and pest control are in other sections, so a reader would think 3-305.11 requires all of them.
issues.correct: "Keep pests out: close doors and report gaps and holes (6-202.15), take out the trash and keep lids on (5-501.113, 5-502.11), keep areas clean and dry with no hiding places (6-501.111), store food covered (3-302.11) and at least 6 inches (15 cm) off the floor (3-305.11)." Put the same citations in keypoints_es[1].

issues.where: beat 7 say_en / say_es / onscreen ("Date labels on ready-to-eat food you keep more than a day")
issues.problem: Date marking (3-501.17) applies only to REFRIGERATED ready-to-eat TCS food that is made on site, or opened from a commercial package, and held more than 24 hours. It can be kept at most 7 days at 41°F or below, and the day it was made counts as day 1. "Ready-to-eat food you keep more than a day" also covers shelf-stable items such as chips or sealed snacks, which do not need a date mark.
issues.correct: say_en: "Date labels on cold ready-to-eat food you keep more than a day." say_es: "Etiquetas con fecha en la comida fría lista para comer que guarda más de un día." If there is room on screen: "7 days max at 41°F; the day you make it is day 1" / "Máximo 7 días a 41°F; el día que se prepara es el día 1".
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 3-501.17 Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking (A), (B)

issues.where: beat 7 say_en / onscreen_en and keypoints (hand sink "soap, paper towels")
issues.problem: The inspector's hand-sink check names paper towels as if they were required. The Code accepts disposable towels, a continuous towel system, a heated-air hand dryer or an air-knife dryer. A stand with a working hand dryer would be wrongly marked as failing.
issues.correct: say_en: "The hand sink: soap, paper towels or a hand dryer, and used only for washing hands." say_es: "El lavamanos: con jabón, toallas de papel o secador de manos, y usado solo para lavarse las manos." Also update the onscreen checklist text.
issues.source: FDA Food Code 2022, 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision (A)–(D); 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser; 5-205.11(B)

issues.problem: "las temperaturas de mantenimiento" reads to most workers as "maintenance temperatures". In the app, "Mantenimiento" is also the name of the repair crew. The question becomes unclear for a low-reading-level audience.
issues.correct: q_es: "En una visita, el inspector revisa a qué temperatura se mantiene la comida fría y la caliente. ¿Cuál es la correcta?"
issues.source: Plain-Spanish clarity; the app labels the repair crew "Mantenimiento" (SUP_PROBLEM_CATS in src/App.jsx)

issues.problem: "el operador autorizado de control de plagas" is a word-for-word copy of "operator". It sounds unnatural, and beat 4's own on-screen text calls the same person "Un técnico de control de plagas", so the lesson uses two names for one role.
issues.correct: Use "el técnico autorizado de control de plagas" everywhere, e.g. objectives_es[1]: "Avisarle al gerente cuando hay plagas y dejar los pesticidas al técnico autorizado de control de plagas."
issues.source: Natural Latin-American Spanish usage; internal consistency with beat 4 onscreen_es

issues.problem: "lugares calientes" means hot places; the English says warm. "Nidos de papel o tela triturada" makes "triturada" agree only with "tela", and it reads stiffly.
issues.correct: "Nidos hechos con papel o tela en pedacitos. Insectos vivos o muertos en lugares tibios, oscuros y húmedos, como debajo del fregadero o detrás del refrigerador."
issues.source: Spanish grammar and meaning match with say_en ("warm, dark, wet places"; "shredded paper or cloth")

issues.problem: "Cada atomizador y cada cubeta lleva una etiqueta" describes what is ("carries a label"). It does not carry the rule in the English, "needs a label".
issues.correct: "Cada atomizador y cada cubeta debe llevar una etiqueta con el nombre del químico." Use the same wording in keypoints_es[4].
issues.source: Meaning match with say_en ("needs a label"); FDA Food Code 2022, 7-102.11

issues.problem: The app screen shows the labels "Temperature logged" and "Problem reported: pests". The real stand portal does not show these words. It shows "✓ Sent to the inspector · N temps" / "✓ Enviado al inspector" and "✅ Submitted!" / "✅ ¡Enviado!". The problem category is "🐜 Pest Control" / "Plagas". An app screen in training should match what staff will actually see.
issues.correct: onscreen_en: "...the phone scans the QR code on the stand poster and shows '✓ Sent to the inspector · 3 temps', then the problem picker with '🐜 Pest Control' tapped and '✅ Submitted!'". onscreen_es: "...muestra «✓ Enviado al inspector · 3 temperaturas», luego el selector de problemas con «🐜 Plagas» marcado y «✅ ¡Enviado!»".
